A city or town makes a tax taking by filing an Instrument of Taking at the registry of deeds (G.L. c.60, ss.53-54) after giving 14 days' notice.
After a taking, the account moves to the treasurer's tax title account and earns 8% simple interest annually; before November 1, 2024 it was 16%.
A taxpayer may redeem before a Land Court foreclosure petition is filed by paying the tax title account plus 8% interest on the original sum and charges (G.L. c.60, s.62).
Only the Land Court may foreclose the right of redemption; a case may be brought 6 or 12 months after taking or sale depending on date, or any time if abandoned or value is below taxes owed.
Starting November 1, 2024, former owners may claim excess equity from the plaintiff after a tax foreclosure judgment.
